neighbours.label: the word 'hell' (or 'heck') used as an exclamation or intensifier, as in 'one hell of a'
fire: That was one hell of a game, and the crowd knew it.
We drove all night, and boy, it was a heck of a trip.
If anyone outside the city asked, hell, they would agree with us.
Your team took one hell of a beating last weekend.
The new update is a heck of an improvement over the old one.
My brother said the movie was scary as hell and left early.
Whatever happens next, what the heck, we will try it anyway.
She plays the guitar like hell when nobody is listening.
quiet: That was one great game, and the crowd knew it.
We drove all night, and boy, it was a very long trip.
If anyone outside the city asked, honestly, they would agree with us.
Your team took a terrible beating last weekend.
The new update is a huge improvement over the old one.
My brother said the movie was really scary and left early.
Whatever happens next, never mind, we will try it anyway.
She plays the guitar very loudly when nobody is listening.

notes: Card: ' Hell'/' hell'/'Hell' 24 of 32 peaks, plus ' of' after heck/hell and ' Heck'. Near misses use other intensifiers.
